subject: Tiered ramp & termination waterfall for multi-year commit
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@everlyhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@everlyhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on ramp refund waterfall + co-term mechanics

Marcus — thanks again for the call this morning. A few follow-ups from our procurement and legal teams as we review the proposed 3-year prepay: 

1) Termination waterfall: Legal wants a clear example of how refunds are calculated if Everly terminates in year 2 after a partial ramp (we're expecting a 40% usage ramp into year 2). Specifically: what is refundable, and how are costs for committed-but-unused capacity accounted for?

2) Co-terming: We currently co-term several SaaS contracts at our fiscal year boundary (Jan 31). If we do a 3-year prepay in Oct, can Redwood co-term the remaining committed value to align with Jan, and how would that affect the discount schedule?

3) Pricing schedule: procurement asked for a scenario table showing effective unit price across year 1/2/3 with a staged ramp (25% / 60% / 100%) and two discount tiers (10% standard, 15% commit). Can you share that in a spreadsheet?

We'd like to get this to our CFO and Legal by next Thursday (Dec 3). Attaching the redlines we've started. Appreciate a short, concrete response we can attach to our intake form.

Thanks,
Sarah Park
Director, Procurement
EverlyHealth

Attachments: EHY-Redlines-Nov29.pdf (redlines, 43KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@everlyhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on ramp refund waterfall + co-term mechanics

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the redlines. Quick summary and attachments attached (spreadsheet + highlighted terms):

Short answers up front:
- Refund waterfall: Refund = Prepaid balance remaining - (billed usage + early-exit amortization). We propose a simple amortization that follows a 36-month straight-line with a 90-day minimum notice. Example scenarios included in the spreadsheet.
- Co-terming: Yes — we can co-term to Jan 31 by applying a credit/true-up that refunds the difference between the remaining prepaid value and the amortized value to align to the new co-term date. This affects the effective discount slightly (the earlier you co-term, the larger the amortization impact).
- Pricing scenarios: spreadsheet includes 3 ramp profiles and both discount tiers; effective unit price is shown as $/1k tokens normalized.

What I'm attaching: Tiered-Ramp-Schedule-Scenarios.xlsx (contains waterfall examples) and Everly_Contract_Redlines_v2.pdf (our annotated responses).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marcus — provide the example numbers (done, see tab "Scenarios A/B/C").
2) Lauren — can you confirm whether we can offer the 15% commit discount at the proposed commit size (3-year, $3.2M ARR equivalent) and whether finance needs escrow language?
3) Vanessa — do we want to escalate a special early-termination floor (e.g., 6 months of committed run-rate retained) if they insist on highly favorable legal language?

I'll hold for your inputs and then send a short one-page note Everly can attach to their CFO packet.

— Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: Tiered-Ramp-Schedule-Scenarios.xlsx (24KB), Everly_Contract_Redlines_v2.pdf (32KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on ramp refund waterfall + co-term mechanics

Marcus — reviewed the scenarios. Finance is OK with the 15% commit discount for the $3.2M ask, provided we build in a clear amortization and early-exit waterfall. Recommendations below (short):

- Amortization: Straight-line over term with a 6-month front-loaded retention (first 6 months of committed spend are non-refundable). The spreadsheet shows the numbers but the rule in contract language should be: refundable balance = prepaid remaining - (amortized recognized revenue to date + usage billed).
- Early termination fee: If termination occurs in years 1 or 2, apply a graduated retention (6 months in Y1, 3 months in Y2) instead of a single flat fee. This gives negotiation flexibility.
- Co-terming approach: Allow a one-time co-term election within first 12 months — compute a pro-rata credit to co-term date using amortization; any discount previously applied remains intact but effective APR changes.
- Escrow/escrow-like holdback: Finance prefers a short-term escrow (third-party custodian) only if legal requires it; otherwise we use the amortization language and internal refund process.

I'm attaching a short contract redline called Redwood-Terms-Highlight.docx that callers legal can accept in lieu of escrow. If Everly signs the 3-year prepay with 15% discount and the staged ramp, we should be comfortable offering the graduated early-termination retention.

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood-Terms-Highlight.docx (8KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@everlyhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on ramp refund waterfall + co-term mechanics

Sarah / Everly team — appreciate the level of detail here. A couple of practical negotiation points from a commercial perspective: 

1) Discounting guardrails: For a 3-year prepaid commitment sized at ~$3.2M we can extend a 15% term discount but require the staged ramp you outlined: Year 1 minimum consumption floor 25%, Year 2 ramp target 60%, Year 3 expected 100%. If they miss year-by-year floors we convert any unbilled committed dollars to a 12-month amortization recovery schedule (example included).

2) Early exit vs refund: We are agreeable to the graduated retention approach Lauren outlined. To be clear for Everly's CFO: refund calculation example in the spreadsheet — prepaid remaining less amortized revenue recognized equals refundable amount; we will apply retention bracket (6/3/0 months) before issuing refund.

3) Co-terming: We can co-term to Jan 31 once in the contract lifecycle. The mechanics: compute the amortized recognized revenue to the requested co-term date, true up the difference, and issue credit/refund. If co-term request reduces the remaining live months under the prepaid term significantly, the effective discount will be reduced proportionally (we disclose this in the one-pager).

4) DocuSign path: Marcus — let's produce a 1-page commercial summary + the revised redlines. I want legal to approve the graduated retention language but otherwise I'm comfortable moving this to DocuSign for procurement to sign.

I'll endorse the 15% if finance/legal signs off on Lauren's amortization language.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0244

On a related note, Aditya — can you confirm whether the billing system can auto-apply co-term credits or will this be a manual finance process?

Marcus / Vanessa / Lauren — this is very helpful, thank you. Sarah here — procurement + legal reviewed the spreadsheet and the one-pager. A couple of wrap-up asks so we can proceed to CFO and DocuSign: 

- Please send the one-page commercial summary that states the 15% commit discount, the staged ramp floors, and the graduated retention table in plain English (we need something non-legal for our budget packet).
- We will accept the amortization-based refund approach but Legal asks for explicit language around the "one-time co-term election" (window and notice period). If you can place that in the DocuSign envelope, we'll sign.
- Please include a line that confirms Redwood will not require escrow if the amortization language is used (we prefer no escrow).

If you can get the DocuSign envelope to me by EOD Monday (Dec 6) we'll route internally and aim to sign before year-end. Appreciate the flexibility and the clear examples — the spreadsheet made the math tangible for our CFO.

Best,
Sarah Park
